data.name: Avernum 5
data.detailed_description:
Avernum is one of the great tales of indie gaming, an epic series of fantasy role-playing adventurers set in an enormous, subterranean nation. Avernum is a land underground, a subterranean nation full of rogues, misfits, and brigands, struggling for survival and wealth in the monster-infested darkness. Avernum 5 is the second chapter in the Great Trials Trilogy, three games that tell the tale of this land’s struggles in the face of powerful forces that seek to destroy it.

Avernum 5 has a fascinating storyline, full of betrayal, mystery, and unexpected turns. Explore a gigantic world, with hundreds of quests, multitudes of side dungeons, and many hours of adventure. The game features clever enemies and dozens of interesting scripted encounters. Learn over 50 spells and battle disciplines. Hunt for hundreds of magical items, or find the materials to craft new, unique equipment.

reviews.review:
Avernum 5 is an old-school role-playing game that proudly embraces the design principles that defined PC RPGs long before cinematic cutscenes and sprawling open worlds became industry standards. Developed and published by Spiderweb Software, the title continues the studio's long-running tradition of delivering expansive adventures built around narrative depth, tactical encounters, and player-driven exploration. Set within the vast subterranean realm of Avernum, the game takes an interesting approach by shifting the player's allegiance, offering a perspective that differs from previous entries in the series and adding fresh context to the world's ongoing political struggles.

The story centers on a dangerous mission assigned by the Empire. A notorious assassin named Dorikas has begun orchestrating events that threaten to plunge the region into chaos, forcing unlikely allies to work together against a common enemy. This premise gives Avernum 5 a stronger focus on investigation and diplomacy than many fantasy RPGs of its era. Throughout the campaign, players encounter rival factions, uncover hidden motives, and influence events through their decisions. The writing remains one of the game's greatest strengths, with extensive dialogue and detailed world-building that make Avernum feel like a believable place rather than simply a backdrop for combat. Those willing to invest time in conversations and side stories will find a surprisingly nuanced narrative beneath the game's modest presentation.

Character development is another area where Avernum 5 excels. Players create and guide a party through a lengthy adventure, shaping each member through a wide assortment of skills, spells, and combat specialties. The customization options encourage experimentation, allowing parties to focus on brute strength, magical prowess, ranged combat, or balanced approaches. Battles unfold in a turn-based format that rewards patience and planning. Positioning, resource conservation, and understanding enemy behavior become increasingly important as the campaign progresses. While the mechanics are relatively straightforward compared to some modern tactical RPGs, they provide enough depth to remain engaging throughout the journey.

Exploration plays a significant role in maintaining the game's appeal. The underground continent is filled with settlements, hidden passages, optional dungeons, and numerous side quests that expand the lore. Spiderweb Software avoids excessive hand-holding, leaving players free to chart their own course and discover secrets at their own pace. This approach can occasionally lead to moments of uncertainty or backtracking, but it also creates a stronger sense of adventure. Every hidden chamber and forgotten ruin feels like a meaningful discovery, reinforcing the impression that Avernum is a world with its own history and inhabitants rather than a sequence of disconnected levels.

Naturally, Avernum 5 shows its age in several respects. Its visuals are functional rather than impressive, with simple character models, limited animations, and environments that prioritize clarity over spectacle. The user interface is easy enough to navigate once learned, though newcomers may find some aspects dated. Audio design is similarly understated, providing atmosphere without becoming a defining feature of the experience. However, these limitations are largely a consequence of Spiderweb Software's independent development philosophy, which consistently favors gameplay systems and storytelling over production values.

Despite its age, Avernum 5 remains a compelling experience for fans of classic computer role-playing games. It understands exactly what it wants to be and rarely deviates from that vision. The combination of an engaging plot, satisfying tactical combat, meaningful exploration, and extensive character customization creates an adventure that can easily occupy dozens of hours. Players expecting modern visuals or streamlined mechanics may struggle to appreciate its charms, but those with an appreciation for traditional RPG design will find a rewarding and surprisingly ambitious title hidden beneath its dated exterior.

Rating: 8/10
